blogs.title: When the Lungs Lie: Unmasking the 'Pulmonary Mask' of Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: This post explores the classic diagnostic pitfall where pediatric pancreatopleural fistula (PPF) masquerades primarily as a thoracic emergency. We analyze why clinicians often default to tuberculosis or primary pneumonia diagnoses when faced with recurrent bloody effusions, despite the pathology originating in the abdomen. The discussion focuses on the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for abdominal etiologies in children presenting with unexplained pleural effusions, especially those with occult abdominal trauma.

blogs.title: The Dark Red Effusion Clue: Differentiating Hemorrhagic Causes Beyond Trauma
blogs.description: Focused on pleural fluid analysis, this entry dissects the specific characteristics of PPF-associated fluid compared to other causes of hemorrhagic pleural effusions like TB, malignancy, or esophageal perforation. We highlight the critical role of pleural amylase/lipase ratios (>1000 IU/L), fluid color changes over time, and the utility of distinguishing between salivary vs. pancreatic isoamylases to rule out mimics and confirm PPF quickly.

blogs.title: Trauma Not Seen: Connecting Bicycle Handle Injuries to Late-Onset Respiratory Failure
blogs.description: Drawing lessons from this specific case, we discuss the phenomenon of delayed presentation following blunt abdominal trauma in children. Since pediatric patients may conceal traumatic events due to fear or lack of awareness, we explore strategies for eliciting hidden trauma histories during repeated admissions for respiratory distress and how even minor mechanisms (e.g., a bicycle accident) can lead to significant pancreatic duct disruption weeks later.

blogs.title: Beyond the Drainage Bag: Algorithmic Management of Pediatric Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: Given the rarity of PPF in pediatrics and lack of consensus guidelines, this article outlines a stepwise management algorithm based on current evidence and this successful case. We compare medical management (NPO, TPN, octreotide) against endoscopic options (ERCP/stenting) and surgery, discussing indications for escalation, expected timelines for resolution (the 'bowel rest' window), and managing complications like malnutrition in growing children.
